title: Overwhelmed with Honor and Joy
primary_topics: Speech at the book launch of 'With Due Respect 3' (WDR3) at the Philippine Daily Inquirer, December 7, 2021 -- CJP's 85th birthday

The origin story of CJP's column-writing career: how Marixi Rufino Prieto convinced a reluctant CJP to write for the Inquirer, and why Salonga's warning ('Chief justices make history. They do not write it') was not the last word
CJP's 15-year unbroken Sunday column streak (February 2007 to December 2021) and the three-volume WDR series published every five years (2011, 2016, 2021)
Tribute to CJ Alexander G. Gesmundo as the book launcher, and to Sean James Borja (WDR3 arranger, 2018 bar topnotcher) as the FLP's poster scholar
sub_topics: The three WDR books: WDR1 (2011), WDR2 (2016), WDR3 (December 7, 2021 -- CJP's 85th birthday); WDR3 is divided into two volumes

CJP's hesitation: never written a column before retirement; had a 'historical romance with newspapers' (peddled them as a student) but never dreamt of writing one; feared the rigors, risks and responsibilities of column-writing vs. legal articles
The Teodoro Valencia connection: CJP was Teodoro Valencia's lawyer -- Valencia was a famous columnist -- and CJP witnessed firsthand the demands of column-writing

Salonga's warning: 'Chief justices make history. They do not write it.' Marixi's counter: 'Dr. Salonga may be correct, but I do not know of any retired chief justice who had been offered to write a column.' They compromised: once a week instead of Marixi's proposed thrice
15-year unbroken streak: February 2007 to December 2021; every Sunday without fail despite illness, 5 foreign trips per year, and duties in 15+ companies and foundations
WDR1 Amazon achievement: third placer in Amazon bestseller list for courts category -- behind Jeffrey Toobin of CNN (1st) and Justice Antonin Scalia (2nd, now deceased)

Libel case: CJP was sued for libel in the 'Disini to pay damages in BNPP suit' column (November 7, 2021); absolutely cleared by DOJ and Court of Appeals which stopped the Makati RTC from hearing the charge as 'completely inane and baseless'

CJ Gesmundo as launcher: at age 65, could be CJP's son; named CJ by President Duterte without seeking it; low profile; abundant competence, integrity, probity and independence; 'glutton for work'; committed to solving case backlog and automating the judiciary

January 2006 Sandiganbayan story: CJ Gesmundo came to CJP's Chamber to take his oath as new Sandiganbayan justice; CJP intuited, 'Please sit on my chair because one day you will be sitting there anyway as chief justice' -- a prophetic act led by the Holy Spirit
Sean James Borja: arranged WDR3 columns topically instead of chronologically; FEU Ateneo valedictorian 2018; numero uno in the 2018 bar exam; multi-awarded mooter; first FLP scholar to sit the bar
JV Rufino: young and energetic boss of Inquirer Books

Inquirer editors: retired Jorge Aruta and Rosario Garcellano; incumbent opinion editor Gilbert Cadiz -- thanked for correcting CJP's 'occasional grammatical errors and failures to observe the Inquirer style book'
signature_phrases: Chief justices make history. They do not write it

they perpetualize my humble work into books every five years

stances.claim: Marixi Rufino Prieto deserves full credit for CJP's opinion-writing career -- not only did she convince a reluctant CJP to write (overcoming Salonga's 'chief justices make history, not write it' warning), but she also compromised on frequency (once vs. thrice weekly) and created the platform that enabled WDR1 to reach the Amazon top-3.
stances.rhetorical_move: patron-attribution: the intellectual career as a gift made possible by a specific patron's insistence

stances.claim: CJP intuitively prophesied Gesmundo's future Chief Justiceship in January 2006 -- 'I had no intention of joking him; I was quite serious. I must have been led by the Holy Spirit to utter those prophesying words without really knowing they will one day be fulfilled' -- framing the appointment of a new associate justice as a moment of divine prophetic disclosure.
stances.rhetorical_move: Holy-Spirit-prophesy framing: the utterance in CJP's Chamber retrospectively validated as charismatic foresight

stances.claim: CJP's column serves the judiciary in ways his SC decisions could not -- with 'more freedom than he had when sitting in the Court bound by its rules and proscriptions,' articulating 'sentiments and views which incumbent members of the Court could only wish to say themselves' (per CJ Gesmundo). The post-retirement column is the superior vehicle for judicial reform advocacy.
stances.rhetorical_move: post-tenure freedom argument: retirement as liberation of judicial voice rather than loss of it
stances.confidence: asserted through CJ Gesmundo's quoted assessment

notable_anecdotes: Marixi vs. Salonga: CJP told Marixi of Salonga's warning -- 'Chief justices make history. They do not write it.' Marixi replied: 'Dr. Salonga may be correct, but I do not know of any retired chief justice who had been offered to write a column.' Compromise struck: once a week instead of the proposed thrice.

The prophetic chair story: in January 2006, when Gesmundo came to CJP's Chamber to be sworn in as a new Sandiganbayan justice, CJP intuitively asked him to sit on his chair and said: 'Please sit on my chair because one day you will be sitting there anyway as chief justice.' -- 'I must have been led by the Holy Spirit to utter those prophesying words.'

The Amazon achievement: WDR1, published in book form by the Philippine Daily Inquirer in January 2012, ranked 3rd on the Amazon bestseller list for courts -- behind only Jeffrey Toobin of CNN (1st) and Justice Antonin Scalia (2nd, now deceased).

Sean James Borja's WDR3 arrangement: instead of chronological columns, Borja arranged them topically 'to give readers a better flavor of the various subjects' -- a structural editorial decision made by the 2018 bar topnotcher.

The libel case: CJP was sued for libel over his November 7, 2021 column 'Disini to pay damages in BNPP suit'; absolutely cleared by the DOJ and the CA which stopped the Makati RTC from hearing the charge as 'completely inane and baseless.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered December 7, 2021 -- CJP's 85th birthday -- at the Philippine Daily Inquirer for the book launch of 'With Due Respect 3' (WDR3), this speech opens with CJP expressing being 'overwhelmed with honor and joy' that Marixi Rufino Prieto and her daughter Sandy Prieto-Romualdez 'perpetualize my humble work into books every five years' -- the third volume in the series (WDR1: 2011, WDR2: 2016, WDR3: December 7, 2021), this time in two volumes. He narrates the origin story: he was deeply hesitant to accept Marixi's invitation to write for the Inquirer, having witnessed firsthand the rigors of column-writing as lawyer to famous columnist Teodoro Valencia, and having never written a column in his life. When he told Marixi of Salonga's warning -- 'Chief justices make history. They do not write it' -- she countered: 'Dr. Salonga may be correct, but I do not know of any retired chief justice who had been offered to write a column.' A compromise was struck: once weekly instead of the proposed thrice. He has written every Sunday without fail for 15 years (February 2007 to December 2021), despite illness, five annual foreign trips, and directorial duties in 15+ companies and foundations. He credits Marixi for the Amazon achievement: WDR1 ranked 3rd on the courts bestseller list behind Jeffrey Toobin (1st) and the late Justice Antonin Scalia (2nd). He discloses that he was sued for libel over his November 7, 2021 'Disini to pay damages in BNPP suit' column -- but was absolutely cleared by the DOJ and the CA. He thanks CJ Gesmundo for launching the book -- a particularly meaningful gesture since CJP intuited in January 2006 (when Gesmundo came to his Chamber to be sworn in as Sandiganbayan justice) that he should sit on the Chief Justice's chair: 'Please sit on my chair because one day you will be sitting there anyway as chief justice. I must have been led by the Holy Spirit.' He thanks Sean James Borja -- Ateneo valedictorian, 2018 bar topnotcher, and FLP's first scholar-bar-sitter -- for arranging WDR3 topically rather than chronologically, JV Rufino (Inquirer Books), and the editorial team, closing with: 'May they never tire of teaching this aging jurist the rudiments of the English language.'
